alex: Quick Q — who is allowed to flip the emergency toggle for model-gateway/llm-experiment-v3? Need to disable traffic right now for a noisy prompt causing a huge cost spike. Also what exactly do I need to put in the audit reason?

taylor: I thought oncall + eng-ml lead. The runbook is fuzzy. @morgan do we require 2-person sign-off for a full prod cutoff?

morgan: Short answer: full production cutoff requires 2 approvals (oncall + eng-ml lead). Partial canary toggles (reduce to 0% for canary audience) can be done by oncall if latency/cost is spiking. Always include incident_id and root_cause in the audit. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/feature-toggle-disable

alex: :thumbsup: can you paste the exact CLI/command? don't want to miss the audit tag.

sam.k: CLI that creates an auditable entry:
```
redwoodctl flags disable --name llm-experiment-v3 --scope prod --reason \"incident:heavy-token-regen\" --incident JIRA-7890
```
If you use the dashboard it will prompt for incident id and force approval flow for full-prod. Note: `--scope canary` won't trigger 2 approvals.

oncall-bot: ALERT: Toggle disable requested by alex. Please confirm by reacting :white_check_mark: or reply with 'approved' within 5 minutes to proceed. Audit ID will be generated.

alex: :white_check_mark: approving now. Incident JIRA-7890. Reason: runaway-cost from image-generation prompt.

taylor: I approve as well. One procedural note: always record model+variant (eg model=redwood-7b-q4) and commit hash that served the model. We need that snapshot if we rollback.

morgan: Added post-action checklist — verify token-rate and latency at +5m and +15m; set temporary rate limit 50rps on gateway to avoid thrash; tag owners in #inc-7890.

alex: Performed disable via CLI, got audit id AUD-20260317-001. Dashboard shows prod=0%, canary unaffected. Metrics look stable. Leaving note in the incident ticket.

oncall-bot: Toggle action logged: AUD-20260317-001 by alex (approved by taylor). Link: https://internal.redwood/audit/AUD-20260317-001

sam.k: :eyes: follow-up suggestion — add a preflight guard that blocks full-prod disable if >3 downstream services depend on the model with no fallback. I will open a small PR (#3142) to add that check.

alex: Thanks everyone — saved a chunk of spend. Filing postmortem checklist items in the incident doc.
